races.name: Racing tv.com/freetrial EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Dream Weddings At Western House Hotel Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Water Of Leith
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's 8-year-old is the race's sole front-runner, wearing headgear, and Paul Mulrennan knows the horse well — a clean break and uncontested lead is its only path to victory, and the style-fit flag tempers expectations if it gets outpaced.|

runners_data.name: Mount Ruapehu
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's 6-year-old has shown consistent prominent racing over 6f on good ground and slots naturally into the race shape just behind the leader, though its recent form figures of 666 suggest it is finding the handicapper's mark awkward.|

runners_data.name: Harlequin Bay
runners_data.note: Richard & Fahey's 3-year-old is a genuine hold-up type with a 34-day break, and while its best form came on standard ground, two placed efforts in recent runs suggest talent that could surface if the pace opens up the straight late.|

runners_data.name: Whiskey Kisses
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope takes the ride on this R Mike Smith 3-year-old, a true closer whose best comparable form was a third on good going over 6f — needs the pace to be fast enough to pull horses back to it, which this race shape may not provide.|

runners_data.name: Cotai Starlight
runners_data.note: Jason Hart partners this Katie Scott-trained 3-year-old, whose best effort was a third over 6f on standard; a genuine hold-up horse in terms of natural style, it has been redistributed to midfield on the map because the rear is congested — it will need to adapt.|

runners_data.name: Royal Duke
runners_data.note: The most course-experienced horse in the field with 12 runs on similar going including 2 wins and 4 places, but a natural hold-up runner placed into a midfield slot by necessity — its record over 5-6f on good ground is the most relevant stat, style compromise aside.|

runners_data.name: Summerstorms Dream
runners_data.note: Lauren Young (5lb claimer) rides Jim Goldie's 4-year-old, which carries the lowest weight in the race; another horse whose instinct is to come from behind, mapped forward on the chart because the hold-up spots are oversubscribed — the style conflict is the central concern.|

races.paceDynamic: Water Of Leith is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival likely to press for the lead, Paul Mulrennan can dictate his own terms down the Ayr straight on good to firm ground. Mount Ruapehu will push forward to track closely from a prominent position, but the pace should remain controlled rather than frenetic, meaning the leaders will not burn out early. Cotai Starlight, Royal Duke, and Summerstorms Dream are all natural hold-up horses redistributed into a midfield mapping because the rear is oversubscribed — none of them is likely to secure a true stalking or closing position, and their style-fit discounts apply. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can be covered up just off a moderate lead and kick on the flat Ayr straight, rather than horses needing a strong pace to chase down.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Water Of Leith sets a sustainable gallop and no rival disrupts the tempo, horses racing prominently in second or third will be perfectly placed to pounce.
scenarios.body: Water Of Leith dictates from the front at a manageable pace, and the horse best positioned just behind — Mount Ruapehu or a prominent tracker — swoops on the straight without needing a searching early gallop to set it up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If Water Of Leith gets away cleanly and Mulrennan nurses a lead that is never seriously threatened, the old campaigner simply outstays the field on fast ground.
scenarios.body: At 8 years old and wearing headgear, Water Of Leith has course experience and a settled mind in front; a truly uncontested lead on good to firm over a track it handles turns this into a straightforward front-running exercise.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Home
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is faster than expected and the front runners tie each other up, a hold-up horse with finishing pace benefits from a strung-out field.
scenarios.body: Whiskey Kisses or Harlequin Bay, the two genuine hold-up runners without redistribution flags, are the only horses for whom this scenario is plausible — but with only one real front-runner, the pace is unlikely to be hot enough to set it up.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Midfield Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Water Of Leith dwells or is outpaced early and the pace is chaotic rather than controlled, redistributed midfield horses scrambling for position could capitalise.
scenarios.body: This is the lowest-probability shape because the redistributed runners — Cotai Starlight, Royal Duke, Summerstorms Dream — are not in their natural style and their style-fit penalties significantly reduce the likelihood they can execute from an unfamiliar position.

watchPoints.text: Water Of Leith's draw and early stride pattern are critical — if it breaks cleanly and Mulrennan can pinch a lead unchallenged, the entire race shape locks in around this horse and prominent runners inherit the best positions.|

Mount Ruapehu has posted three consecutive sixth-place finishes and is in danger of going off again at an unfavourable odds-to-form ratio; watch whether Andrew Mullen commits forward or drops it out, as that decision shapes where the race's modest tempo sits.|

The trio of Cotai Starlight, Royal Duke, and Summerstorms Dream are all hunting for a position in the rear that the race cannot comfortably supply — early traffic and positional friction on the near side of the field is a genuine risk in the first furlong.|

Whiskey Kisses and Harlequin Bay are the only two horses without redistribution or style-fit flags in the hold-up section; if either is able to get a clean run on the wide outside in the straight, they represent the most structurally sound closing threat in the race.|

Good to firm ground at Ayr today — confirmed across every race on the card — suits a straightforward pace scenario and makes a fast-finishing closer's task harder; the surface reading reinforces the premium on a well-positioned, prominent tracking run.|

races.name: 25% Off Lunch At Western House Hotel Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Supreme Dancer
runners_data.note: Fahey-trained 3yo who is a genuine hold-up type but maps to midfield here due to the volume of closers in the field; modest recent form (form string 557-28) and just 10 from 14 runs on similar ground with no wins, though Warren Fentiman's 3lb claim offers a marginal weight concession.|

runners_data.name: Lanarra
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on standard ground and placed on good most recently, but this 7f trip at Ayr represents an extra furlong for a horse whose profile suggests a sprint-trip specialist; naturally runs from the rear but the crowded hold-up group means she'll be tucked in further than suits, and connections must hope the step up in trip brings improvement.|

runners_data.name: Ramon Di Loria
runners_data.note: Veteran 8yo who is the only confirmed pace-setter and will have the run entirely on his terms; five of his last five runs feature mid-pack finishes over 6-7f on good ground, but his style data tags him as Prominent — he should stride into a clear lead and the question is whether he conserves enough to hold on, as his form (636332) shows consistent placed efforts rather than winning ones at this level.|

runners_data.name: Soul Warrior
runners_data.note: Consistent warning sign here — flagged for fading in the finish — and despite a win to his name this season over 6f on soft, he steps up to 7f on quicker ground; Alex Jary's 3lb claim is a mild positive, but the finish-fade flag and the fact he's a true hold-up horse pushed into midfield mapping combine to dampen optimism for a bold showing in the straight.|

runners_data.name: Imperial Guard
runners_data.note: Brings the strongest profile for this race shape: won over 7f on good ground (1W3P in 10 runs on similar going) and is reunited with Daniel Tudhope, one of the most capable jockeys in this field; ran just 7 days ago suggesting fitness is live, and with the highest carried weight (145lbs) reflecting his OR of 60, he is the class act of the hold-up brigade in a race that sets up for his running style.|

runners_data.name: Yaaser
runners_data.note: Aged 8 and wearing a hood, Jim Goldie's sprinter-miler has a deeply uninspiring recent form string (997595) with zero wins from six runs on good ground in his last 15 outings on similar surfaces; the 11-day turnaround is fine, but Mulrennan will need a significant step forward from this consistent non-winner.|

races.paceDynamic: Ramon Di Loria is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no rivals likely to seriously contest the lead, he will stride forward from the gate and control tempo at a measured, sustainable gallop over this 7f trip on good-to-firm ground at Ayr. The five hold-up types behind him — Imperial Guard, Yaaser, Supreme Dancer, Lanarra, and Soul Warrior — will be forced to track at varying distances, creating a compact mid-to-rear grouping with limited positional variety. Because the field holds more genuine hold-up horses than the race shape can differentiate, Supreme Dancer, Lanarra, and Soul Warrior are mapped forward of their natural position; in reality they are likely to settle deeper, leaving Imperial Guard and Yaaser as the closest chasers from the hold-up pack. A lone, uncontested front-runner dictating on a flat, fair course at a comfortable clip strongly favours hold-up horses with late finishing ability on this ground — specifically those who have demonstrated the class and consistency to close from off a genuine pace, with Imperial Guard's proven record over 7f at Ayr making him the archetype of the beneficiary.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Ramon Di Loria dictates an uncontested, honest pace that neither collapses nor accelerates excessively, setting up a genuine test for closers.
scenarios.body: Ramon Di Loria bowls along in front unchallenged, allowing him to conserve energy through the middle sector before kicking again inside the final 2f; the hold-up horses get a reliable target to aim at and those with the strongest finishing gear cut him down close home.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swamps Them
scenarios.trigger: If Ramon Di Loria sets an unexpectedly slow early pace, creating a bunched field where a well-handicapped closer can sprint past the entire field in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The compressed tempo means no horse is truly stretched until the dash for home, and a horse with raw speed and a sharp turn of foot finds the gaps opening up quickly on the fast surface.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Ramon Di Loria sets a moderate but sustainable gallop and the closers are blocked or slow to respond turning for home.
scenarios.body: Ramon Di Loria has shown consistent front-running form over 7f on good ground — five of his last six runs have featured placed or front-tracking efforts — and a field of genuine hold-up horses that are mapped out of position may find themselves arriving too late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Ramon Di Loria goes off too fast and ties up early, leaving a scramble among the hold-up pack who are all racing further back than ideal.
scenarios.body: The redistributed hold-up horses — Supreme Dancer, Soul Warrior, Lanarra — are forced to cover extra ground from their deeper positions, and with Soul Warrior's noted tendency to fade in the finish, the race devolves into a scrappy finish among those who can quickest find daylight.

watchPoints.text: Imperial Guard (Tudhope) to be tracked from the outset — if he's travelling smoothly approaching the 2f pole, he is the most dangerous closer in a race set up by Ramon Di Loria's uncontested front-running.

Ramon Di Loria's fractions matter critically — if he is allowed to bowl along at a very slow gallop, the hold-up horses lose their target and the race shape inverts into a sprint finish that suits no one clearly.

Soul Warrior is flagged as a horse that fades in the finish — if he moves up menacingly early in the straight, monitor whether he sustains the effort or drops away sharply, as backing him late could be deceptive.

The going report confirms 7f at Ayr as Good To Firm — faster than the stated card going of Good — which will sharpen finishing speeds and may slightly benefit horses with proven fast-ground form (Imperial Guard: 1W3P on similar).

Three apprentice jockeys (Fentiman, Jary) are in the field — if any of the hold-up horses are held up deeper than mapped in a small field of six, there is a real risk of traffic issues late if Ramon Di Loria slows the early pace and the bunch converges simultaneously.

races.name: Fergie & Myra Happel Ayr Gold Cup Trial Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Veblen Good
runners_data.note: Lone front-runner in the race; Tudhope and O'Meara have the tools to control this, and a win over 6f good ground in recent form is a positive, though a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93 notes it is racing slightly out of its most natural role and its finishing kick may be vulnerable to fresh prominent challengers late.

runners_data.name: Lord Roxby
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with two wins from 15 runs on good ground and solid course form over 6f; Alex Jary (3lb claim) keeps the weight down at 134lbs, and five of the last five career runs have been over 6f on good, making this trip-and-going combination his most familiar environment.

runners_data.name: Gentle George
runners_data.note: Three-year-old from R Mike Smith's yard, just nine days since last run which bears monitoring for freshness, though the yard has two winners from 14 in the past fortnight; has won over 6f on soft and placed over 6f good, but the 18th-of-18 over 5f on good last time out raises a question about current form consistency.

runners_data.name: Jordan Electrics
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old veteran hold-up horse for Jim Goldie running just three days after his last start, which is a significant workload flag; a fade-in-finish warning accompanies his profile, and while he has placed over 6f on good ground in his recent history, age and the short turnaround make this a difficult winning ask.

runners_data.name: Azure Zain
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up racer who won over 6f on good ground in his last five runs and holds form figures of 3-5-0-1-6; Warren Fentiman's 3lb claim helps at 127lbs, and 29 days since last run gives him a fresher profile than several rivals, though only 5 of 13 career runs on similar ground have produced a placed finish.

runners_data.name: Clonmacash
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner wearing a visor; Adrian McGuinness sends him over from Ireland nine days since last run, and he has placed four times from 15 on good ground including a recent third and fourth over 6f, suggesting consistency without quite finding the winner's enclosure at this level.

runners_data.name: Oriental Prince
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's hold-up horse at OR 71, the lowest rated in the field; a 20th-of-20 over 7f good last month is deeply concerning, and only five of his last 15 runs on similar ground have produced a place, with no win in recent form — the drop back to 6f is a marginal help but not enough to reverse the trajectory.

runners_data.name: Dandy Magic
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse by profile — four of his last five runs have produced mid-pack finishes — whose true rearward position is unlikely to be achievable here with only one confirmed pace-setter; Lauren Young (5lb claim) is positive, but only three of 15 runs on comparable going have placed, and the redistribution discount reflects the structural mismatch between his natural style and this race's pace.

runners_data.name: The Caltonian
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with a fade-in-finish flag who won his last race over 6f on standard ground but has struggled on good, placing in only three of 15 comparable-going runs; Andrew Mullen rides for Linda Perratt (no winners in the last 17 days), and his hold-up style faces the same structural constraint as Dandy Magic — a single front-runner sets too modest a pace for a true closer to generate winning momentum from the back.

races.paceDynamic: Veblen Good is the lone confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner 6f handicap on good-to-firm ground at Ayr, and with no genuine rival likely to press for the lead, Daniel Tudhope should be able to control tempo from the front without being pressured into an unsustainably fast gallop. That controlled, honest pace over 6f on quick ground typically sets up a race where prominent racers can travel in the slipstream and pounce, rather than one that is truly run to suit deep hold-up horses. Lord Roxby, Gentle George, and Clonmacash all carry prominent racing styles that place them well to benefit from sitting just off Veblen Good's shoulder and striking when the pace is pegged back rather than red-hot. The field nominally contains more hold-up horses than the shape can accommodate — Dandy Magic and The Caltonian are genuine hold-up types who have been redistributed to midfield on the map because they are unlikely to secure their natural rearward position given the lack of genuine strong pace to chase — which further dilutes the viability of a late-closing scenario. **Tactical verdict: the race shape strongly favours the prominent-racing profile — horses that can sit a length or two off Veblen Good, make smooth headway at the 2f pole, and sustain their effort on the fast surface through the final furlong.**

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Veblen Good leads at a sustainable gallop and the prominent holders track and overhaul in the final 2f.
scenarios.body: Veblen Good sets a measured tempo that keeps the race within reach of those just behind, and runners like Lord Roxby and Gentle George, tracking just off the pace, get a clean run to challenge as the field straightens; on good-to-firm ground over 6f the horse that controls energy expenditure from a prominent position is hardest to peg back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Veblen Good Converts
scenarios.trigger: If Veblen Good is allowed to dictate at a genuinely comfortable tempo and steals a winning advantage turning for home.
scenarios.body: O'Meara's sprinter has shown a win over 6f on good ground in its recent history and, if rivals are slow to respond or get stuck in traffic, an uncontested lead on a fair surface can be remarkably hard to reel in over this trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Swooper Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is faster than anticipated and prominent horses empty, allowing a midfield runner to pick up the pieces late.
scenarios.body: A stronger early clip would string the field out and leave a window for a horse like Azure Zain — who won over 6f on good ground — to close powerfully from a tracked midfield position; Jordan Electrics has shown ability at this course-and-distance level, though the fade flag tempers expectations.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If the race is run at a genuinely strong gallop and the true closers are able to produce a sustained finish from the rear.
scenarios.body: Dandy Magic and The Caltonian are both natural hold-up types, but both carry redistribution and style-fit discounts because they are unlikely to get far enough back to generate meaningful late momentum in a race with only one front-runner; the scenario is possible but structurally improbable given the pace map.

watchPoints.text: Veblen Good leads unchallenged — if Tudhope engineers a comfortable lead with no rival pressuring, watch whether Gentle George or Lord Roxby have enough in hand to close the gap in the final furlong on this quick surface.

Jordan Electrics runs just three days after his last outing — watch his behaviour in the preliminaries and early strides for any sign that the short turnaround has taken an edge off his travelling, as a horse already flagged for fading in the finish can ill-afford extra fatigue.

Dandy Magic and The Caltonian — both true hold-up horses mapped to midfield — will likely find themselves in a no-man's land if the pace is modest; watch whether their jockeys attempt to push forward early or accept a position that suits neither their natural style nor the race shape.

Azure Zain is the freshest horse in the field at 29 days since last run; on quick ground over 6f with a 3lb claiming jockey, watch whether he gets a clean passage from the rear into midfield around the 3f pole, as his one win in this form-cycle came over this exact trip and going.

races.name: John Hamilton ScotRail Celebration Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Mayor Of Maghera
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with strong course-relevant good-ground form including a win over 9f at Goodwood, trained by R Mike Smith who has had two winners from 14-day runners; a genuine hold-up horse by style who will find himself racing closer to the pace than ideal in this compressed field, potentially limiting his finishing kick.|

runners_data.name: Starliner
runners_data.note: Five-year-old veteran who has been busy (7 days since last run) and wears a visor; her best form comes from further back but the crowded hold-up section means she will not get an unobstructed passage from her natural position — her seven good-ground runs have produced only one win and three places, suggesting she needs everything to go right.|

runners_data.name: Keep Me Stable
runners_data.note: Six-year-old prominent racer with a strong record at 7f on good ground (two wins in last five at that trip), stepping up to a mile here for Linda Perratt; 14 days since last run is ideal freshness, and the flat Ayr mile should suit a horse who travels prominently and stays competitive, though her wins have come at shorter.|

runners_data.name: Donna Nook
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with a course-winning profile — won at 8f on good ground — trained by O'Meara whose 3-from-44 over 14 days is steady rather than electric; wears tongue-tie and visor, has placed consistently at this distance, and will be one of the more capable hold-up horses if she can settle properly in a race with a compressed rear section.|

runners_data.name: Benacre
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with a modest recent sequence (355054) who has failed to win in six good-ground starts and wears a hood; Charlie Johnston has runners in form (7/65 over 14 days) but Benacre's own profile offers limited grounds for confidence at OR 72 and this distance without a recent win at 8f or beyond.|

runners_data.name: Runninsonofagun
runners_data.note: Four-year-old in a career-best moment — won last time at 8f on good ground — trained by Tristan Davidson who has 3 from 12 recent runners in decent form; wears blinkers and is a natural hold-up horse forced forward by race shape, so his ability to maintain the rhythm he had last time may depend on how the early pace unfolds.|

runners_data.name: Hale End
runners_data.note: Six-year-old confirmed front-runner who carries top weight at OR 75 and has won and placed multiple times at 8f on good ground — the sole genuine pace-setter in this field giving him full control of the tempo; the STYLE_FIT tag notes he is slightly out of role as a prominent type carrying the pace alone, and his record of not winning when the pace scenario reverses is worth noting.|

runners_data.name: Krissy
runners_data.note: Five-year-old prominent racer with an excellent recent record — four wins from nine good-ground starts including a win at 9f on good ground — partnered by 5lb claimer Rhys Elliott which brings her weight down; Jim Goldie has five winners from 65 runners recently and Krissy's profile as a consistent, travelling prominent type makes her ideally suited to shadowing Hale End and producing a sustained effort.|

runners_data.name: Cisco Disco
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old who has recorded his two recent wins at 10f on softer ground, and whose last five runs on good going have been modest (10th, 8th, 8th prominent); dropping back from preferred longer trips and conditions represents a significant ask, and while Paul Mulrennan is an experienced rider at Ayr, the form profile here is one of the more concerning in the field.|

races.paceDynamic: Hale End is the confirmed front-runner here and, as the sole genuine pace-setter in a nine-runner field, will dictate from the gates on good to firm ground over Ayr's flat mile, setting a sustainable rather than pressured tempo. Krissy and Keep Me Stable will be drawn into prominent positions and are likely to track Hale End closely through the early stages, meaning the pace will be honest but not frenetic. The field holds more hold-up and prominent types than the race map can accommodate at the rear — Mayor Of Maghera, Starliner, and Runninsonofagun are genuine hold-up horses by profile but will be forced to race closer to the pace than ideal, compressing the field and reducing the likelihood of a meaningful late rattle from true closers. A moderate, controlled gallop with Hale End pulling the strings and a compressed midfield suits horses who can travel prominently and produce a sustained finish from a tracking position — Krissy and Keep Me Stable are best placed to benefit from this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hale End Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Hale End bowls along unchallenged and the field settles into a compact, strung-out procession behind him.
scenarios.body: Hale End sets a metronomic pace on a flat track with no sustained pressure, and the race becomes a test of which prominent tracker can sustain their effort into the straight most effectively. Horses who can travel economically just off the pace — saving energy early and producing a clean, sustained finish — are the clear beneficiaries of this controlled shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pressures Lead
scenarios.trigger: If Keep Me Stable or Krissy push forward aggressively early and force Hale End into a faster-than-anticipated gallop.
scenarios.body: A contested pace on good to firm ground over a flat mile will stretch the field and expose those who waste energy in a scrappy early battle, but will simultaneously set up the race for horses with a genuine turn of foot in the final two furlongs. Front-runners who do not quicken will be caught, and the horse who settles best just behind the pressure — likely Donna Nook or Runninsonofagun if they get a rhythm — will hit the line strongest.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong throughout and the front group ties up inside the final furlong, creating a gap for a late finisher.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires the displaced hold-up types — Mayor Of Maghera, Starliner, Cisco Disco — to navigate traffic from further back than their natural positions allow, which is a meaningful ask given the redistribution context. Cisco Disco's declining form at shorter trips makes this harder to envisage, though Mayor Of Maghera has the form credentials on good ground if everything falls right.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Defies Field
scenarios.trigger: If Hale End builds an unassailable lead with no runner able to close the gap in the straight.
scenarios.body: On fast ground Hale End has the highest OR in this field and a proven record of winning at this trip, and a truly muddling pace from an unchallenged solo lead could see the field never close the deficit. However, Krissy's prominent profile and strong recent form represent the most obvious threat to this outcome, and a solo win from the front is the least likely resolution given the competitive prominent contingent tracking.

watchPoints.text: Krissy and Keep Me Stable — both prominent types will attempt to press Hale End closely from early, and how quickly they establish position will define whether the pace is truly controlled or develops into a tempo that burns off the front end.

Mayor Of Maghera, Starliner, and Runninsonofagun are genuine hold-up horses being displaced forward by field dynamics — watch whether they settle in the mid-division or get shuffled wider on the flat Ayr track, as either outcome changes their ability to produce a clean finish.

Hale End's weight (135lbs, top of the handicap) on a quick surface over a flat mile — if he does soften in the closing stages, it will happen quickly given the lack of undulation at Ayr to help him regulate effort.

Cisco Disco's preference for 10f and softer ground is a notable mismatch — watch whether Paul Mulrennan opts to restrain him sharply or attempts to cover more ground early, as neither suits the profile.

Rhys Elliott's 5lb claim on Krissy is a meaningful weight reduction in a competitive handicap — watch whether the inexperience of a claiming rider affects Krissy's positioning behind Hale End in the early stages of a race where fractional advantages matter.

races.name: Try Racing TV For Free Now Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Motawaared
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for Jim Goldie who has shown modest form at 12f on good ground (sim-going record 7/11, 0 wins), and the step up in trip has not yet unlocked improvement — Paul Mulrennan's booking is a slight positive but the horse is yet to show it can win off this OR.|

runners_data.name: Taylormade Lad
runners_data.note: Michael Dods-trained four-year-old whose sim-going figures (7/13, 1W3P) are decent and two recent third-place finishes at 11f on good suggest the 1m2f trip and conditions suit — Sean Kirrane picks him up fresh off a 17-day break and hood is noted.|

runners_data.name: Falcon Nine
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's six-year-old carries a hood and has two wins from 15 similar-going starts, but its natural racing style is true hold-up — in this one-paced-gallop scenario it will likely find itself in a pack of similarly-displaced closers rather than the rear it prefers, which tempers its chance.|

runners_data.name: Braes Of Doune
runners_data.note: The race's only genuine front-runner, Jim Goldie's eight-year-old has a strong sim-going record (12/15, 2W7P) and will lead uncontested — Lauren Young's 5lb claim is useful, but its recent form figures of 66 and a 7-day turnaround mean the question is whether it has the reserves to hold on.|

runners_data.name: Toy Soldier
runners_data.note: Four-year-old trained by Russell & Scudamore who is a natural closer but will find itself shuffled into midfield rather than settled at the rear; two second-place finishes on good ground are encouraging, yet the congested midfield position undermines what it does best.|

runners_data.name: Glasses Up
runners_data.note: Eleven-year-old veteran for R Mike Smith who won over 13f on good last time out — Clifford Lee retains the ride and the horse has a solid sim-going record (12/15, 1W2P), but it too is a hold-up type racing in a compressed pack rather than off the back of the field.|

runners_data.name: Sophiesticate
runners_data.note: Another R Mike Smith hold-up performer whose recent form shows consecutive third-place finishes at 12f on good; the 1m2f trip suits and the sim-going record (8/15, 1W6P) is respectable, yet Shay Farmer (5) takes over and the horse is being shoehorned into midfield rather than hunting from the rear as it prefers.|

runners_data.name: Phantom Shadow
runners_data.note: Ewan Whillans' three-year-old showed promise at 10f on good going (2nd, 3rd) and carries 5lb less than older rivals — Jason Hart's experience could prove key if the horse gets a prominent berth close to Braes Of Doune, though form at 1m2f specifically is limited.|

runners_data.name: Golden Valour
runners_data.note: Decade-old R Mike Smith inmate whose best sim-going run was a third at 8f; stepping up from 7-9f trips to 1m2f looks a stretch in trip terms, and Rhys Elliott's claim is its main attraction — essentially a market outsider displaced from its preferred stalking role.|

runners_data.name: Wadacre Geisha
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's three-year-old has a consistent record at 10f on good going, with multiple placed efforts (sim-going 5/7, 0W2P) suggesting she handles these conditions — Andrew Mullen rides and her all-good-ground form is a plus, but she is boxed into midfield rather than the prominent position her talent arguably warrants.|

runners_data.name: On The Bubble
runners_data.note: Gary Rutherford's five-year-old heads into this on just a 5-day turnaround and trainer's T14 record of 0/4 is a red flag; an all-good-ground horse with placing habit but no wins, it is squeezed into midfield when it naturally wants to settle at the rear, making a competitive effort hard to envisage.|

races.paceDynamic: Braes Of Doune is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, is set to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 1m2f on good-to-firm ground at Ayr. With one horse setting the fractions unchallenged, the early pace is unlikely to be punishing, meaning the race will not naturally string out — the pace-setter creates a compact, measured contest where the winner will need to pick up off a modest tempo rather than simply survive a gruelling test. The overwhelming majority of this field are natural hold-up or prominent horses, and with so many sharing the same profile, the midfield will be congested and positional battles inevitable inside the final quarter-mile. This race shape strongly favours horses who can race handily just behind the leader and produce a sustained run rather than a late burst from deep, since the moderate gallop set by Braes Of Doune will leave genuine closers with little ground to make up — but also little wall of tired horses to come through. Note that the field holds significantly more prominent and hold-up types than can physically secure their natural position: Falcon Nine, Toy Soldier, Wadacre Geisha, Glasses Up, Sophiesticate, Golden Valour and On The Bubble are all natural hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map, but in reality several will be racing further back than ideal; Braes Of Doune and, to a lesser extent, Taylormade Lad and Phantom Shadow are best placed to secure the prominent berths that matter here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Braes Of Doune Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Braes Of Doune leads uncontested and sets a steady-to-moderate gallop that keeps the field together into the straight.
scenarios.body: Braes Of Doune controls every yard, and horses who can race in behind without having to change gears dramatically into a sprint finish are best suited — a sustained, front-running or prominently-ridden effort from the front two or three pays off on this track.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challengers Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If one or two horses pressing Braes Of Doune from the outset grind the front-runner down in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The pace is still not strong, but a horse sitting second or third and travelling comfortably has the energy to collar the leader before the line; this favours runners who naturally want to be close to the action and have the scope to extend at 1m2f.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is faster than anticipated or the front runners tie each other up, creating enough pace to set up a late run.
scenarios.body: A closing run from a horse with genuine finishing speed becomes viable only if the tempo lifts; even then, the redistributed hold-up horses face the dual problem of being forced into unfamiliar midfield positions and needing a pace collapse that this single front-runner set-up rarely produces.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Rank Outsider Poaches Prize
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so slow it turns into a sprint and a shorter-priced runner gets first run at a completely flat-footed field.
scenarios.body: A horse who secures a prominent position cheaply and quickens first from the turn-in can steal what becomes effectively a 2f dash; this scenario depends entirely on the pack being caught napping in a slowly-run race.

watchPoints.text: Braes Of Doune's ability to hold on matters enormously — watch whether Lauren Young (5lb claim) can control the pace at 1m2f after a 7-day turnaround; if the horse ties up in the straight the race opens up dramatically.

Phantom Shadow is the one three-year-old in the field and carries less weight — watch Jason Hart's positioning from the gate, because if he slots in second or third early he is the most dangerous challenger to the front-runner given 10f good-ground form.

Wadacre Geisha's all-good-ground Ayr-trip profile is the best in the race on paper — watch how Andrew Mullen deploys her from the pack, as she has a habit of finishing second and could do so again if she gains a prominent position.

R Mike Smith runs three horses (Glasses Up, Sophiesticate, Golden Valour) — watch for any in-running traffic problems as they will all be looking to come from midfield, and their presence could cause interference in a bunched straight.|

Taylormade Lad's hood and 17-day freshness for Michael Dods are worth noting — Sean Kirrane often travels prominently and could put this horse in a useful second or third position early, making it a live each-way factor in Scenario B.|

runners_data.name: Brash
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up performer for David & Nicola Barron whose recent form includes a solid second over 6f on Good; dropping to 5f is worth monitoring given two of last five runs came over longer, but Good to Firm going is fine and William Pyle's 3lb claim is a small asset.

runners_data.name: Golden Havana
runners_data.note: Mike Dods runner who wants to come from off the pace — visor fitted to sharpen focus — but with multiple hold-up types in this field, Sean Kirrane will be forced to race closer than Sean would choose; sim-going record of 2 from 11 in similar conditions is modest.

runners_data.name: Sea Her Excel
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on Good ground and has placed three times at 5f on Good; Elle-May Croot's 5lb claim helps at the weights, and her style — hold-up but not extreme — means she is among the better-placed of the closers to find a position just off the leader.

runners_data.name: Under The Radar
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's three-year-old has an excellent record at 5f on Good ground (3-1-3 in 9 starts) and was only four days ago, which demands monitoring; a genuine closer by inclination who will be squeezed forward by the shape of this race, reducing his ability to produce a late rattle.

runners_data.name: Bella Delizia
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner, and crucially the only horse with a structural reason to secure the lead unchallenged; won over 5f on Good and her Ayr-similar course form (3 from 7 on Good/Firm) is encouraging, with Alex Jary's 3lb claim softening the weight ask for Nigel Tinkler.

runners_data.name: Sands Of Seve
runners_data.note: Won over 5f on Soft and has a second at 5f on Good — best form is at this trip — but wears a visor today and Gary Harrison's yard is 0 from 3 in the last 14 days; a hold-up horse who will be pushed into a midfield role, blunting the late-run weapon he relies upon.

runners_data.name: Brain Freeze
runners_data.note: Won over 5f on Good ground for Michael Dods and wears a hood; three of his last five starts on Good produced a win and two places, so the going is no issue, but as a genuine hold-up type bumped into midfield by the congestion, his typical closing run will be compressed and harder to execute.

races.paceDynamic: Bella Delizia is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 5f Ayr sprint and, with no rival likely to seriously dispute her for the lead, she should dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset rather than being forced into an overly hot early pace. The remainder of the field — Golden Havana, Under The Radar, Sands Of Seve, Brain Freeze, Brash, and Sea Her Excel — are all natural hold-up or wait-and-pounce types, meaning Bella Delizia gets a free rail and a rhythm of her own choosing on Good to Firm ground that will suit a leader travelling comfortably. This field holds significantly more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate at the rear; Golden Havana, Under The Radar, Sands Of Seve, and Brain Freeze are all true closers who will be forced to race closer to the pace than their natural style demands, with Bella Delizia and, to a lesser extent, Sea Her Excel the most likely to secure their preferred early position. The uncontested pace, flat track, and fast ground combine to strongly favour a horse that can control the tempo and sustain it to the line — the front-running and prominent profile has a decisive structural advantage here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bella Delizia Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Bella Delizia leads uncontested from the gate and sets a fair but not excessive gallop on the Good to Firm surface.
scenarios.body: She dictates every yard on a flat track, conserves energy through the early stages, and her rivals — forced to race closer than ideal — lack the sprint finish to peg her back. Horses who can race prominently or who have the class to close on a controlled pace are best placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Pick Up Late Ground
scenarios.trigger: If Bella Delizia sets an honest enough gallop that the back-markers, despite racing out of their natural role, find a genuine late run.
scenarios.body: The compact 5f trip and good ground mean the early pace, though fair, still burns enough petrol that horses with a turn of foot can rattle home; those with better form on similar going have the edge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Mid-Race
scenarios.trigger: If Bella Delizia's early lead is so dawdling that the field compresses and a bunched sprint develops in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A wall of horses hits the line together and those drawn or positioned best at the two-furlong mark benefit most; any horse with a peak TS burst on Good to Firm can emerge from the pack.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Fades, Hold-Ups Swamp
scenarios.trigger: If Bella Delizia goes too hard in the absence of pressure and ties up inside the final furlong, gifting the race to the field.
scenarios.body: True hold-up types would benefit most but several are racing out of position here, limiting the likelihood of a clean finish; those with the best form at the trip still have the best chance of profiting.

watchPoints.text: Bella Delizia is the only horse with a clear run at an uncontested lead — watch whether she gets away cleanly from the gate, because any early stumble or slow break could fundamentally alter the entire race shape.

Under The Radar runs just four days after his last start; watch him in the paddock and early in the race for any sign of staleness or reluctance that could confirm the short turnaround has blunted his form.

With Golden Havana, Under The Radar, Sands Of Seve, and Brain Freeze all forced closer than ideal, watch for significant early crowding and scrimmaging behind Bella Delizia in the first furlong that could unsettle multiple runners simultaneously.

Sands Of Seve and Golden Havana both wear headgear (visor) today — watch whether the gear sharpens their early pace and pushes them even closer to Bella Delizia than their natural style suggests, which could tighten the lead scenario materially.

Sea Her Excel's trainer Ivan Furtado is 4 from 29 over the last 14 days — a low-but-active strike rate — so watch whether the market reflects any stable confidence ahead of the off given she is among the best-positioned of the hold-up types here.
